root.claim: There is a deterministic fixed multitape Turing machine multiplying $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: build two fast tape procedures, use them for synthetic and resampled transforms, and assemble the exact product through convolution

motivation.text: The Schoenhage-Strassen style product is a convolution, and fast transforms cost n log n only because of movement and butterflies, so power savings on those two operations give a power saving overall.

root.salient: The saving is a power $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ of the logarithm, not just a factor of $\log\log n$, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$ tiny.

children.claim: Two tape procedures, an address interchange of cost $O(Vu^\tau)$ and a simultaneous butterfly layer of cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, exist for volume $V$ with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$.
children.method: build both from fixed linear networks with a rank saving, applied recursively

motivation.text: Scanning the whole array at each of the log n transform levels already costs n log n, so movement and arithmetic must both be made cheaper than a scan per level; a recursion whose normalized cost grows by a factor below the parameter gives a power saving.

children.salient: The recursion multiplies cost by s/W strictly below m per level, giving a power saving with exponent strictly below 1.

motivation.text: An edge matrix of rank a requires only a smaller interchanges once it is factored, so the rank saving of the network turns into a recurrence saving a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: Normalized synthetic transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ can be computed and inverted with the frequency order retained, using the parallel layers.
children.method: use powers of $y$ as roots of unity and compute with radix-two butterflies on a layout fitting the parallel layers

motivation.text: Multiplication by a root of unity becomes a signed shift, so only butterflies cost arithmetic, and those are exactly what the simultaneous layer accelerates.

children.claim: Sums of powers of the synthetic roots of unity cancel, so the transform and its opposite invert each other up to a scale.
